story.title: Evacuations Ordered in Nepal Following Budhi Gandaki Flash Flood
story.summary: Nepal's authorities have ordered evacuations for residents along the Budhi Gandaki River after a landslide triggered a flash flood on October 11. The flood has swept away homes and buildings in the mountainous north-central region of the country.
sources: AP - Top News via Google News

timeline_highlights.title: Flash Floods in Nepal and Tibet Leave Hundreds Dead and Thousands Missing
timeline_highlights.summary: Devastating flash floods triggered by a glacier collapse have affected the Nepal-Tibet border, resulting in nearly 600 deaths and leaving approximately 1,900 people missing. Rescue operations are ongoing, with teams facing challenges due to the risk of further flooding from a rising lake formed by the disaster. Among the missing are at least 33 British nationals and numerous tourists from over 30 countries, prompting families to rush to the region in search of their loved ones.
key_facts: Flash floods caused by glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border.
Death toll estimated at nearly 600, with around 1,900 people missing.
Rescue efforts are complicated by the risk of additional flooding.
At least 33 British nationals among those missing.

revisions.title: Flash Floods in Nepal and Tibet Leave Hundreds Missing, Including Tourists
revisions.summary: Severe flash flooding in Nepal has resulted in the disappearance of hundreds of individuals, including 291 international tourists. Rescue efforts have been hampered by high floodwaters, preventing helicopters from reaching affected areas. Among those reported missing are at least three American tourists, contributing to a preliminary total of 384 missing persons.

timeline_highlights.summary: Rescue teams in Nepal are concentrating their efforts on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe many workers may be trapped. This comes two weeks after severe flooding resulted in over 1,300 fatalities and left approximately 5,000 individuals missing, including foreigners. The floods have affected both Nepal and the Tibet region of China.

timeline_highlights.title: Flash Floods Prompt Evacuations in Northern Nepal
timeline_highlights.summary: Residents in northern Nepal have evacuated their villages due to flash flooding from the Budhi Gandaki River. The floods have reportedly swept away several buildings and bridges, exacerbating the situation in an area already affected by previous catastrophic floods two months prior.
key_facts: Flash floods from the Budhi Gandaki River have led to evacuations in northern Nepal.
Several buildings and bridges have been swept away by the floods.
This event follows catastrophic floods that occurred two months earlier.

event_overview.title: About Nepal Floods
event_overview.subject: Nepal Floods
event_overview.summary: The Nepal floods refer to the catastrophic flash-flood disaster that began on 26 August 2026 in northern Nepal’s Bhotekoshi–Trishuli river corridor. The event caused major loss of life and damage to communities, transport links, hydropower facilities, and border infrastructure, prompting a Government of Nepal-led emergency and recovery response supported by UN and humanitarian partners.

facts.label: Start date and status
facts.value: The flash floods began on 26 August 2026; emergency relief was followed by a four-month humanitarian appeal, while longer-term recovery continued beyond the immediate response period.

facts.label: Main affected area
facts.value: The core impact area was northern Nepal, particularly Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems; damage also affected transport, trade and tourism connections near the Nepal–China border.

facts.label: Hazard mechanism
facts.value: UN material describes the disaster as a cascading mountain-hazard event triggered by a large rock-ice avalanche in the high Himalaya, which generated destructive flash floods downstream.

facts.label: Response leadership
facts.value: Nepal’s disaster response was led by the Government of Nepal, including the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority and the Ministry of Home Affairs, with UN agencies, the Red Cross movement and other partners supporting coordination and relief.

facts.label: Seasonal context
facts.value: The event occurred during Nepal’s June-to-September monsoon season, when heavy rainfall commonly increases flood and landslide risk across the country.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-August 2026 acute disaster phase—casualty and missing-person reports, rescue operations and immediate cross-border impacts—not the full history of flooding in Nepal or the subsequent recovery and reconstruction process.

related_stories.title: New York City Police Use-of-Force Review Ordered by Mayor Mamdani
related_stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has ordered a review of the New York Police Department's use-of-force policies, marking the first such review in a decade. This decision comes amid calls for greater police reform, although city officials state that it is not directly related to a recent police response to an ICE shooting. The review aims to address concerns raised by progressive advocates regarding police practices.

related_stories.title: Hurricane Simon Strikes Mexico's Pacific Coast, Causing Flooding and Damage
related_stories.summary: Hurricane Simon has weakened to a Category 3 storm but continues to impact Mexico's Pacific coast with strong winds and heavy rainfall. The storm has caused significant flooding in homes and has affected resorts and vulnerable towns along the coastline.

related_stories.title: South Africa's Deputy Police Chief Resigns Amid Sexual Offense Charges
related_stories.summary: Shadrack Sibiya has resigned from his position as South Africa's deputy police chief following serious allegations, including charges of sexual offenses. He has denied accusations of grooming a 16-year-old and raping an 18-year-old. Sibiya was previously suspended amid corruption allegations.
